code: rt <- cpt_runtimes rt$cell <- ifelse(rt$status == "ok", format(round(rt$seconds, 2), nsmall = 2),                   rt$status) wide <- reshape(as.data.frame(rt[, c("method", "n", "cell")]),                 idvar = "method", timevar = "n", direction = "wide") names(wide) <- c("method", "1e3", "1e4", "1e5", "1e6")[seq_along(wide)] wide[is.na(wide)] <- "" fastest <- rt[rt$n == 1e6 & rt$status == "ok", ] # Fastest at a million first, then the rest alphabetically. rank_1e6 <- match(wide$method, fastest$method[order(fastest$seconds)]) wide <- wide[order(is.na(rank_1e6), rank_1e6, wide$method), ] knitr::kable(wide, row.names = FALSE,              caption = "Seconds per fit (blank: not attempted)")

title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: single changepoint detection method dominates across signal shapes, noise regimes, computational budgets: large-scale evaluations find ranking algorithms highly dataset-dependent default configurations often far optimal (van den Burg Williams 2020; Truong et al. 2020). Sound practice therefore requires running several detectors, comparing outputs, , ground truth available, scoring well-defined accuracy metrics. article presents comparison evaluation toolkit ggchangepoint: visual comparison across methods (ggcpt_compare()), common tidy representation competing segmentations (ggcpt_compare_table()), metrics module implementing precision/recall/F1 one--one matching, covering metric, Hausdorff distance, adjusted Rand index (cpt_metrics()), multi-annotator scoring style Turing Change Point Dataset benchmark (cpt_metrics_annotated()), visual evaluation ground truth (ggcpt_eval()). discuss three complementary tools quantifying uncertainty segmentation: engine-native confidence intervals, bootstrap stability profiles (cpt_stability()), CROPS penalty path (cpt_crops()). close small simulation-based benchmarking workflow built package’s ground-truth generators.

title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: changepoint literature offers wide menu detectors (penalised optimal partitioning, binary segmentation wild narrowest--threshold refinements, moving-sum statistics, nonparametric divergence measures, Bayesian posteriors), inductive bias (Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017; Truong et al. 2020). Benchmarks score many algorithms many series find uniform winner: performance depends kind change (mean, variance, distribution), noise (Gaussian, heavy-tailed, autocorrelated), number spacing changes, tuning penalties thresholds (van den Burg Williams 2020). Two practical consequences follow. First, analyst compare several methods data hand rather trust one default. Second, ground truth (expert annotation) exists, comparison quantitative, using metrics agreed conventions. ggchangepoint supports activities behind one interface. Every detector returns tidy ggcpt object, competing methods directly comparable; comparison module renders side side, evaluation module scores . article package’s methods-paper treatment workflow. companion vignette vignette("introduction", package = "ggchangepoint") documents full detection surface; take detectors given focus comparison, evaluation, uncertainty.

text: ggchangepoint provides unified, tidy, ggplot2-native interface changepoint detection R: one dispatcher (cpt_detect()) covering 50 methods across six methodological families, one result class (ggcpt) stable tidy contract, one visualisation entry point (autoplot()) draws everything method reports, including confidence intervals posterior probabilities (Wickham 2016; Robinson 2017). vignette feature tour: visits every exported function package point belongs workflow, reader can map full surface one sitting. title: The ggchangepoint Feature Tour: A Complete Map of the Package Surface
text: Multiscale inference confidence. smuce_wrapper() implements SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014), bounds probability -estimating number changes level alpha returns confidence interval every changepoint location (ci_lower/ci_upper); family = "hsmuce" switches heteroskedastic extension HSMUCE (Pein et al. 2017), estimates variance per segment: Change slope. cpop_wrapper() performs exact penalised estimation continuous piecewise-linear mean (Fearnhead et al. 2019; Fearnhead Grose 2024): Bayesian detection. bcp_wrapper() implements Barry-Hartigan product-partition model (Barry Hartigan 1993; Erdman Emerson 2007); bocpd_wrapper() runs Bayesian online changepoint detection run-length posterior (Adams MacKay 2007); beast_wrapper() wraps BEAST Bayesian model-averaging ensemble (Zhao et al. 2019). first third keep locations whose posterior probability clears prob_threshold record posterior_prob column; BOCPD returns maximum posteriori changepoint set. Sequential kernel nonparametrics. cpm_wrapper() runs distribution-free sequential tests reports, alongside estimated location, detection_time stream monitor flagged (Ross 2015); kcp_wrapper() applies kernel change point analysis running statistics (mean, variance, autocorrelation, correlation) (Arlot et al. 2019; Cabrieto et al. 2018); npmojo_wrapper() detects distributional changes serial dependence (McGonigle Cho 2025): Robustness drift dependence. decafs_wrapper() detects abrupt changes signal also drifts noise autocorrelated (Romano et al. 2022); sn_wrapper() segments chosen parameter (mean, variance, autocorrelation, bivariate correlation) self-normalisation, avoiding long-run variance estimation entirely (Zhao et al. 2022); envcpt_wrapper() reports changepoints changepoint model beats trend autoregressive alternatives (Beaulieu Killick 2018): High-dimensional multivariate. wrappers take matrix data frame one row per time point. inspect_wrapper() finds sparse mean changes projection (Wang Samworth 2018); ocd_wrapper() monitors high-dimensional stream online (Chen et al. 2022); geomcp_wrapper() maps observation distance angle segments (Grundy et al. 2020); multivariate ecp input flows cpt_detect() unchanged. univariate wrappers, contrast, reject multi-column argument rather silently flattening . Regression structure. strucchange_wrapper() dates Bai-Perron breaks, either bare series coefficients formula (Bai Perron 1998, 2003; Zeileis et al. 2002); segmented_wrapper() fits continuous broken-line regression, change reports kink trend rather jump level (Muggeo 2003, 2008). carry confidence interval every break: modern PELT family. fastcpd_wrapper() exposes fastcpd engine, whose family argument covers changes mean, variance, , well changes fitted AR/ARMA/GARCH model (Li Zhang 2024):
code: res_smuce <- smuce_wrapper(x, alpha = 0.5) tidy(res_smuce) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>      cp cp_value ci_lower ci_upper #>   <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> #> 1   100    0.369      100      100 set.seed(5101) y_slope <- cumsum(c(rep(0.4, 100), rep(-0.3, 100))) + rnorm(200) res_cpop <- cpop_wrapper(y_slope) tidy(res_cpop) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1    99     40.8 res_bcp <- bcp_wrapper(x, seed = 1) tidy(res_bcp) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value posterior_prob #>   <int>    <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369              1 res_bocpd <- bocpd_wrapper(x) tidy(res_bocpd) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 res_beast <- beast_wrapper(x, seed = 1) tidy(res_beast) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value posterior_prob #>   <int>    <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369              1 tidy(cpm_wrapper(x, cpm_type = "Mann-Whitney")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value detection_time #>   <int>    <dbl>          <int> #> 1   100    0.369            105 tidy(kcp_wrapper(x, running_stat = "mean", nperm = 100, seed = 1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   101     7.22 tidy(npmojo_wrapper(x)) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 #> 2   122    8.13 tidy(decafs_wrapper(x)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 tidy(sn_wrapper(x3, parameter = "mean")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100   -0.100 #> 2   199    5.53 res_env <- envcpt_wrapper(x, models = c("mean", "meancpt", "trendcpt")) tidy(res_env) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 res_env$penalty$type   # criterion and winning model #> [1] "AIC: meancpt" set.seed(1) X <- cbind(a = c(rnorm(80), rnorm(80, 4)),            b = c(rnorm(80), rnorm(80, -3)),            c = rnorm(160)) res_hd <- inspect_wrapper(X) tidy(res_hd) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value strength #>   <int>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1    80   -0.590     30.8 # Online detection: the reported locations are declaration times (the change # plus the detection delay), in a `declared_at` column. Monte Carlo threshold # calibration makes this the slowest wrapper, so it is shown but not run # here. It needs at least two coordinates and rejects a univariate series. res_ocd <- ocd_wrapper(X, mc_reps = 100) tidy(res_ocd) tidy(geomcp_wrapper(X)) #> # A tibble: 0 × 2 #> # ℹ 2 variables: cp <int>, cp_value <dbl> tidy(cpt_detect(X, method = "ecp", seed = 1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1    80   -0.590 tidy(strucchange_wrapper(x)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>      cp cp_value ci_lower ci_upper #>   <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> #> 1   100    0.369       99      101 tidy(segmented_wrapper(y_slope, npsi = 1, seed = 1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>      cp cp_value ci_lower ci_upper #>   <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> #> 1    99     40.8       98      101 tidy(fastcpd_wrapper(x, family = "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369

text: autoplot() renders ggcpt. Options: show_segments (fitted segment means), show_fit (engine’s fitted signal, provided; nine engines cpt_methods() marks fitted column: SMUCE, HSMUCE, CPOP, bcp, BEAST, DeCAFS, segmented, mcp, bfast), show_ci (changepoint-location confidence intervals, provided; seven marked ci column: SMUCE, HSMUCE, strucchange, segmented, mcp, bfast, taylor; nsp marked reports region, drawn show_regions), show_points/show_line, index date axis, cptline_* styling arguments (cptline_color, cptline_alpha, cptline_type, cptline_linewidth). Asking overlay result supply warns rather failing silently.   Multivariate results facet automatically:  composable layers work inside ggplot pipeline: geom_changepoint() draws vertical rules, geom_cpt_segment() draws segment levels, geom_cpt_ci() draws horizontal interval whiskers, stat_changepoint() runs detection inside plot. theme_ggcpt() publication theme annotate_segments() shades alternating segments.    ggcptplot() ggecpplot() original one-call plots two classical engines:   Bayesian engines get field’s signature displays: ggcpt_posterior() shows posterior mean series per-location changepoint probability (bcp BEAST results); ggcpt_runlength() shows BOCPD run-length posterior heatmap.   Finally, ggcpt_interactive() turns result (ggplot built one) plotly widget values hover. widget embedded , class:
code: autoplot(res, show_segments = TRUE, cptline_color = "firebrick",          cptline_type = "dashed", cptline_linewidth = 0.8) autoplot(res_smuce, show_ci = TRUE, show_fit = TRUE) autoplot(res_hd) cp_tbl <- tidy(res) df <- data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x)  ggplot(df, aes(index, value)) +   annotate_segments(cp = cp_tbl$cp, n = length(x)) +   geom_line() +   geom_changepoint(data = cp_tbl, aes(xintercept = cp), color = "red") +   geom_cpt_segment(     data = res$segments,     aes(x = start, xend = end, y = param_estimate, yend = param_estimate),     inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "darkred", linewidth = 1   ) +   theme_ggcpt() ggplot(df, aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   stat_changepoint(method = "pelt", color = "blue") ci_tbl <- tidy(res_smuce) ci_tbl$y_pos <- min(x) - 1 ggplot(df, aes(index, value)) +   geom_line(color = "grey60") +   geom_cpt_ci(     data = ci_tbl,     aes(y = y_pos, xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper),     width = 0.6, color = "blue", inherit.aes = FALSE   ) +   geom_changepoint(data = ci_tbl, aes(xintercept = cp), color = "blue") ggcptplot(x, change_in = "mean", cp_method = "PELT") ggecpplot(x, algorithm = "divisive", seed = 1) ggcpt_posterior(res_bcp) ggcpt_runlength(res_bocpd) class(ggcpt_interactive(res))   # requires plotly #> [1] "plotly"     "htmlwidget"

text: cpt_simulate() (alias rcpt()) generates series known changepoints mean, variance, , slope, Gaussian, Student-t, AR(1), random-walk noise; truth travels data true_changepoints true_segments attributes. Five canonical test signals literature ship ready-made: signal_blocks() (Donoho-Johnstone blocks signal (Donoho Johnstone 1994)), signal_fms(), signal_mix(), signal_teeth(), signal_stairs().
code: sim <- cpt_simulate(300, changepoints = c(100, 200), change_in = "mean",                     params = c(0, 5, 1), seed = 1) attr(sim, "true_changepoints") #> [1] 100 200 sim2 <- rcpt(300, changepoints = 150, params = c(0, 3), seed = 2)  # the alias attr(sim2, "true_changepoints") #> [1] 150  signals <- list(blocks = signal_blocks(1024, seed = 1),                 fms    = signal_fms(500, seed = 1),                 mix    = signal_mix(500, seed = 1),                 teeth  = signal_teeth(400, seed = 1),                 stairs = signal_stairs(500, seed = 1)) vapply(signals, function(s) length(attr(s, "true_changepoints")), integer(1)) #> blocks    fms    mix  teeth stairs  #>     11      7      5      3      9 blocks <- signals$blocks ggplot(blocks, aes(index, value)) +   geom_line(color = "grey50") +   geom_vline(xintercept = attr(blocks, "true_changepoints"),              color = "blue", linewidth = 0.3) +   labs(title = "The blocks test signal with its true changepoints")

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: ggchangepoint provides unified, tidy interface changepoint detection across methodological spectrum. introduces single S3 result class, ggcpt, broom-style methods (tidy(), glance(), augment()) (Robinson 2017), central dispatcher cpt_detect() covering 50 detection methods across six algorithmic families, native ggplot2 (Wickham 2016) visualisation autoplot() set composable geoms. method quantifies uncertainty (simultaneous confidence intervals SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014), break-date intervals Bai-Perron (Bai Perron 1998), posterior distributions Bayesian detectors (Barry Hartigan 1993; Adams MacKay 2007)), result object carries uncertainty plotting layer can draw . package supplies penalty-path diagnostic (CROPS), batch detection panels series, bootstrap stability diagnostics, accuracy metrics aligned current benchmarking conventions (van den Burg Williams 2020), ground-truth simulation, per-method citations. article sets statistical background, design package, method family turn, worked examples throughout.

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: Changepoint analysis (locating instants stochastic behaviour ordered sequence changes) one oldest problems statistics, dating back least continuous-inspection schemes Page (1954), one active: recent surveys catalogue dozens methods (Truong et al. 2020; Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017). applications span virtually every domain produces sequential data, including genomics (Picard et al. 2005), finance (Athey et al. 2022), climate science (Haslett Raftery 1989), signal processing (Lavielle 2005). R ecosystem mirrors breadth. Penalised optimal partitioning lives changepoint (Killick Eckley 2014) fpop (Maidstone et al. 2017); wild binary segmentation wbs breakfast (Fryzlewicz 2014, 2020); multiscale inference stepR (Frick et al. 2014); Bayesian analysis bcp (Erdman Emerson 2007) ocp (Adams MacKay 2007); structural breaks strucchange (Zeileis et al. 2002); . packages excellent , returns different object, follows different indexing convention, draws (draw) plots. analyst wants compare PELT segmentation Bayesian posterior multiscale confidence set (routine task applied work) must therefore learn several APIs, reconcile several conventions, write custom plotting code . ggchangepoint removes friction. design goals : One vocabulary. single front door, cpt_detect(x, method, change_in, penalty, ...), whose arguments mean thing every engine. One result type. Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tidy contract, whatever upstream engine returned. One rendering path. Every result (point estimates, confidence intervals, fitted signals, posteriors, penalty paths) draws autoplot() extends ordinary ggplot2 layers. Wrap, don’t reinvent. detection delegated peer-reviewed upstream engines; optional engines live Suggests loaded requested.

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: complementary family locates changepoints scanning test statistics. Binary segmentation (Scott Knott 1974; Vostrikova 1981) recursively splits series maximal CUSUM statistic; wild binary segmentation (Fryzlewicz 2014) successor WBS2 (Fryzlewicz 2020) draw random subintervals short segments masked; narrowest--threshold () (Baranowski et al. 2019) favours narrowest interval contrast exceeds threshold, generalises cleanly changes slope; MOSUM (Eichinger Kirch 2018) scans moving-sum statistic fixed bandwidth, across range bandwidths; Isolate-Detect (Anastasiou Fryzlewicz 2022) isolates changepoint expanding interval; TGUH (Fryzlewicz 2018) performs tail-greedy bottom-merge. SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014) occupies special place: estimates step function fewest jumps still passes simultaneous multiscale test level α\alpha, delivers confidence intervals every changepoint location, uncertainty statements competitors make. HSMUCE (Pein et al. 2017) extends heterogeneous noise.

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: Changes need mean: change_in argument accepts "mean", "var", "meanvar", "slope", "distribution", "covariance", "network", "regression" "seasonality", nine values cpt_methods() lists supports column, routable methods declare . Nonparametric engines (energy statistics (Matteson James 2014), nonparametric cost functions (Haynes et al. 2017), kernel running statistics (Arlot et al. 2019; Cabrieto et al. 2018), joint characteristic functions (McGonigle Cho 2025), self-normalisation (Zhao et al. 2022)) detect distributional change without likelihood assumptions; Bayesian engines (Barry Hartigan 1993; Adams MacKay 2007; Zhao et al. 2019) return posteriors instead point sets; high-dimensional engines (Wang Samworth 2018; Chen et al. 2022; Grundy et al. 2020) aggregate evidence across coordinates; regression engines (Bai Perron 1998; Muggeo 2003) date breaks model coefficients. tour visits family runnable code.

Univariate methods likewise refuse multi-column input rather flattening . Penalty semantics differ across engines, cpt_penalty() documents constructs standard values: Two warrant word. "sSIC" strengthened Schwarz criterion k(log⁡n)αk (\log n)^{\alpha}, α=1.01\alpha = 1.01 default (Fryzlewicz 2014), marginally heavier BIC, criterion search-based engines apply internally. "MBIC" cpt_penalty() returns 0.5(k+1)log⁡n+log⁡(nk)0.5 (k+1) \log n + \log \binom{n}{k}: BIC-type term plus combinatorial cost placing kk changepoints among nn observations. deliberately stronger "BIC", modified BIC Zhang Siegmund (2007), whose penalty 1.5klog⁡n+0.5∑ilog⁡(ℓi/n)1.5 k \log n + 0.5 \sum_i \log(\ell_i / n) depends segment lengths ℓi\ell_i therefore written function nn kk alone; quantity changepoint package computes character penalty "MBIC". Character penalties ("MBIC", "BIC", …) pass changepoint-family engines natively resolved numeric values functional-pruning engines (fpop, cpop, decafs). Search-based engines (WBS, , MOSUM, …) select models ignore argument, engines tuned significance level, posterior-probability threshold, average run length (SMUCE, bcp, BEAST, CPM, SNSeg).

code: set.seed(5301) series <- list(   a = c(rnorm(60), rnorm(60, 4)),   b = c(rnorm(80), rnorm(80, 2)),   c = c(rnorm(70), rnorm(70, 6)),   d = c(rnorm(100, 0, 3), rnorm(100, 9, 3)) ) labels <- list(   a = as_cpt_labels(60, n = 120),   b = as_cpt_labels(80, n = 160),   c = as_cpt_labels(70, n = 140),   d = as_cpt_labels(100, n = 200) ) model <- cpt_learn_penalty(series, labels, penalties = 2^(0:10)) model #> ggcpt_penalty_model (native interval regression) #>   Trained on 4 series with method `pelt` #>   Features: log_n, log_log_n, log_sd, log_mad, log_range, log_sd_diff, log_mad_diff, log_q90_abs_diff #>  #> Coefficients (predicting log penalty): #>        intercept            log_n        log_log_n           log_sd  #>           3.7140          -0.3358          -0.1005           0.4148  #>          log_mad        log_range      log_sd_diff     log_mad_diff  #>           0.4245           0.3636           0.3031           0.3735  #> log_q90_abs_diff  #>           0.2757  #>  #> Use it directly: cpt_detect(x, method = "pelt", penalty = model) predict(model, series$d) #> [1] 347.4859 cpt_detect(series$d, method = "pelt", penalty = model) #> ggcpt (changepoint detection result) #>   Method:             pelt #>   Change in:          mean #>   Changepoints found: 1 #>   CP convention:      left #>   Penalty:            Manual = 347.49 #>   Series length:      200 #>  #> Changepoints: #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    -1.55 cpt_penalty(model, series = series$d) #> [1] 347.4859 nrow(cpt_detect(series$d, method = "pelt")$changepoints) #> [1] 32 nrow(cpt_detect(series$d, method = "pelt", penalty = model)$changepoints) #> [1] 1 cpt_learn_penalty(series, labels, penalties = 2^(0:10),                   engine = "native")$fit$engine #> [1] "native"

title: Autoplot a ggcpt object — autoplot.ggcpt
text: object ggcpt object. show_segments Logical. Whether draw fitted segment means. Defaults FALSE. show_ci Logical. Whether draw confidence intervals changepoint locations, engine provides (columns ci_lower/ci_upper changepoints tibble, supplied engines cpt_methods() marks ci column: smuce, hsmuce, strucchange, segmented, mcp, bfast taylor). nsp marked well drawn argument: reports region_start/region_end rather interval around estimate, show_regions draws. Drawn horizontal whiskers near bottom panel. Defaults FALSE. show_fit Logical. Whether draw engine's fitted signal (fitted column $data, provided engines cpt_methods() marks fitted column: smuce, hsmuce, cpop, bcp, bocpd (causal running mean), beast, decafs, segmented, envcpt, mcp bfast, plus every formula fit). Defaults FALSE. show_regions Logical. Whether shade significance regions interval-valued method returns (regions slot; currently nsp_wrapper()). band interval contains least one changepoint stated global level; confidence interval around point estimate. Defaults TRUE result carries regions, ignored otherwise. cptline_alpha Alpha changepoint lines. Defaults 1. cptline_color Color changepoint lines. Defaults "blue". cptline_type Linetype changepoint lines. Defaults "solid". cptline_linewidth Linewidth changepoint lines. Defaults 0.5. show_points Logical. Whether draw data points. Auto-500 obs. show_line Logical. Whether draw line. Defaults TRUE. index Optional vector x-axis values (e.g. dates) length series. Defaults time index carried result (see index argument cpt_detect()), observation position none. labels Optional cpt_labels() tibble. supplied, labelled regions shaded behind series coloured outcome cpt_label_error() gives (correct, false positive, false negative), scoring segmentation expert labels becomes picture rather table. drawn multivariate result, warns instead. type view draw. "series" (default) series changepoints; "statistic" "path" delegate ggcpt_statistic() ggcpt_solution_path(), error list supporting engines one expose internals. "scale_space" delegates ggcpt_scale_space(), needs nothing engine: sweeps multiscale detector series, draws result. "diagnostics" residual check fit four panels: residuals segment boundaries (structure left behind), autocorrelation per segment (independence engines assume), normal Q-Q plot per segment (Gaussian cost) spread segment (constant variance); cpt_gof() gives checks numbers. ... Unknown arguments ignored warning, except type "series", case passed delegate.

title: Sequential change point model wrapper (CPM) — cpm_wrapper
text: Wraps cpm::processStream() (Ross, 2015) distribution-free sequential changepoint detection via repeated two-sample tests (Mann-Whitney location, Mood scale, Lepage, Kolmogorov-Smirnov Cramer-von-Mises general changes, parametric Student/Bartlett/GLR variants). title: Network-structure changepoints via non-negative matrix factorisation — fabisearch_wrapper
code: # \donttest{ # A change in *structure*, not in scale: two latent factors drive # different halves of the node set before and after the change. # Deliberately tiny: this is by far the most expensive engine in the # package (n_runs x n_reps factorisations per candidate split). Measured # at 5-6 s across fresh sessions, against 27 s for the 2 x 25 / # n_reps = 4 # version this replaced, and this is the floor: `n_reps = 1` fails # inside fabisearch with "not enough 'x' observations" (the permutation # test needs two), and smaller matrices are not reliably cheaper because # the search then evaluates more splits relative to `min_dist` (2 x 10 at # min_dist = 8 measured 6.6 s). So this one example stays near CRAN's 5 s # budget by necessity; `cran-comments.md` says so. Use the defaults on # real data; the settings here are for the budget, not for detection. set.seed(2026) block <- function(n, cols) {   f <- abs(stats::rnorm(n)) + 0.5   Y <- matrix(abs(stats::rnorm(n * 5)) * 0.2 + 0.1, n, 5)   Y[, cols] <- Y[, cols] + f   Y } Y <- rbind(block(12, 1:2), block(12, 3:5)) fabisearch_wrapper(Y, min_dist = 10, n_runs = 1, n_reps = 2,                    alpha = 0.25, rank = 2) #> ggcpt (changepoint detection result) #>   Method:             fabisearch #>   Change in:          network #>   Changepoints found: 1 #>   CP convention:      left #>   Penalty:            engine alpha = 0.25 #>   Series length:      24 #>  #> Changepoints: #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1    12    0.754 # }

title: ggchangepoint package — ggchangepoint-package
text: ggchangepoint provides consistent S3 result class (ggcpt) changepoint detection results, broom-style methods (tidy(), glance(), augment()), ggplot2 integration via autoplot() composable geoms (geom_changepoint(), geom_cpt_segment(), geom_cpt_ci(), geom_cpt_region(), geom_cpt_label(), geom_cpt_event(), stat_changepoint()), unified dispatcher cpt_detect() reaches fifty methods. Detection engines. cpt_detect() dispatches methods cpt_methods(), across nine families: Penalised/optimal: PELT, BinSeg, SegNeigh, AMOC     (changepoint); FPOP (fpop); fast binary segmentation     (binsegRcpp); CROPS penalty path (cpt_crops());     fastcpd (fastcpd, incl. AR/ARMA/GARCH); change--slope via     CPOP (cpop). Multiscale/search: WBS (wbs), WBS2 TGUH     (breakfast), (), MOSUM incl. multiscale     (mosum), Isolate-Detect (IDetect), SMUCE/HSMUCE     confidence intervals (stepR), WBS nonstationary series     (wbsts). Inference: Narrowest Significance Pursuit (nsp),     returns intervals rather points. Nonparametric/kernel: NP (changepoint.np),     E-Divisive/E-Agglo (ecp), kernel running statistics     (kcpRS), NP-MOJO (CptNonPar), sequential CPM (cpm),     self-normalisation (SNSeg), depth ranks     (KWCChangepoint). Bayesian: Barry-Hartigan posterior (bcp), online     BOCPD (ocp), BEAST model averaging (Rbeast),     formula-based regression changepoints (mcp). High-dimensional: sparse projection     (InspectChangepoint), online ocd (ocd), geometric mapping     (changepoint.geo), sparsity-adaptive ESAC Pilliat     (HDCD), covariance, network, VAR     high-dimensional-regression changes (changepoints). Functional network: functional mean covariance     (fChange), NMF-based network structure (fabisearch). Regression, trend season: Bai-Perron breaks CIs     (strucchange), broken-line regression (segmented),     changepoints-vs-autocorrelation model selection (EnvCpt),     drift+AR robust detection (DeCAFS), BFAST season--trend     breaks (bfast). Classical single-change tests: Pettitt, Buishand     SNHT (trend), Taylor's analyzer (ChangePointTaylor). surrounds detectors. Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tibble(cp, cp_value) contract, optionally carrying time index, engine confidence intervals, fitted signal, significance regions diagnostics. Around : fit: cpt_families() (Poisson, binomial,     exponential costs), formula regression break     (cpt_detect(y ~ x, data)), cpt_segment_models()     predict() model per regime. big, , whether : cpt_effect(),     cpt_test_at() (date fixed advance),     cpt_attribute_event(), cpt_test_null(),     cpt_null_power(). believe : cpt_assumptions(),     cpt_gof(), cpt_robustness(), cpt_verify(). Inference: cpt_confint() (four provenances, one     contract), cpt_test(), cpt_regions(). Choosing K: cpt_select() (BIC, Zhang-Siegmund     mBIC, AIC, CROPS elbow, cross-validation, stability),     cpt_crops(), cpt_penalty(). Diagnostics: cpt_influence(), cpt_leverage(),     cpt_sensitivity(), cpt_stability(),     cpt_statistic(), cpt_solution_path(),     cpt_scale_space(). Supervised detection: cpt_labels(),     cpt_label_error(), cpt_label_error_curve(),     cpt_learn_penalty(). Choosing method: cpt_recommend(),     cpt_consensus(), ggcpt_compare(). Evaluation: cpt_metrics(),     cpt_metrics_annotated(), cpt_benchmark(),     cpt_datasets(), cpt_load_tcpd(). Streaming: cpt_monitor(), cpt_update(),     alarms(), cpt_replay(), cpt_delay(). Study design: cpt_simulate(), cpt_power(),     cpt_min_detectable(), cpt_scenarios(). Communication: cpt_annotate_events(),     cpt_report(), cpt_gt(), ggcpt_interactive(),     cpt_cite(). Extension: as_ggcpt()     cpt_register_method() bring detectors package     depend grammar. Leaving R: as_json(), cpt_export(),     cpt_import(). Measurements: cpt_runtimes,     cpt_invariances, cpt_noise_benchmark,     cpt_data_types, cpt_null_sizes,     cpt_calibration. Every condition package raises classed; see ggchangepoint-conditions.

title: SMUCE / HSMUCE wrapper: multiscale changepoint inference — smuce_wrapper
text: Wraps stepR::stepFit() Simultaneous MUltiscale Changepoint Estimator (SMUCE) Frick, Munk Sieling (2014) heterogeneous extension HSMUCE (Pein, Sieling Munk, 2017). SMUCE estimates step function subject simultaneous multiscale test level alpha; level bounds probability -estimating number changepoints, fit delivers confidence intervals every changepoint location, populate ci_lower/ci_upper columns result render via autoplot(show_ci = TRUE) geom_cpt_ci().

title: SMUCE / HSMUCE wrapper: multiscale changepoint inference — smuce_wrapper
text: x numeric vector. alpha Significance level multiscale test \((0, 1)\); smaller values yield conservative (fewer-changepoint) fits. Defaults 0.5, upstream recommendation estimation. family Noise model: "gauss" (SMUCE, homogeneous Gaussian noise), "hsmuce" (HSMUCE, segment-wise variance), "poisson" (counts: change rate) "binomial" (0/1 outcomes: change probability). Defaults "gauss". two count families run stepR::smuceR(), multiscale estimator exponential families, level jump intervals; cpt_detect(x, method = "smuce", family = "poisson") reaches . stepR documents smuceR() deprecated working, route families stepFit() gains ; removed, error says names methods fit family. alpha given, smuceR() takes threshold asymptotic null distribution rather simulated one. remaining stepR families ("jsmurf", "mDependentPS", ...) require filter covariance specification; call stepR::stepFit() directly . "hsmuce" additionally refuses series whose point--point variation lies seven orders magnitude scale: globally flat series, step whose segments numerically constant, cpt_simulate(sd = 0) produces rounding added. stepR's heterogeneous variance estimator aborts R session input rather raising error, caught. "gauss" handles whole range. ... Additional arguments passed stepR::stepFit() (stepR::smuceR() count families).

Eighteen new wrappers, whose engines live CRAN enter Suggests behind requireNamespace() guards: smuce_wrapper(): SMUCE/HSMUCE multiscale inference (stepR), first engines populate ci_lower/ci_upper confidence-interval columns. cpop_wrapper(): exact change--slope detection (cpop); cpt_detect(change_in = "slope") now routes ’s linear contrast instead erroring. bcp_wrapper(), bocpd_wrapper(), beast_wrapper(): Bayesian pillar (bcp, ocp, Rbeast), posterior_prob columns posterior mean carried fitted signal. cpm_wrapper(): sequential distribution-free detection (cpm), detection_time column. kcp_wrapper(): kernel change point analysis running statistics (kcpRS; mean, variance, autocorrelation, correlation). npmojo_wrapper(): nonparametric MOSUM serial dependence (CptNonPar). decafs_wrapper(): abrupt changes amid drift AR(1) noise (DeCAFS). sn_wrapper(): self-normalised segmentation (SNSeg; mean, variance, acf, bivariate correlation). inspect_wrapper(), ocd_wrapper(), geomcp_wrapper(): high-dimensional multivariate detection (InspectChangepoint, ocd, changepoint.geo). strucchange_wrapper(): Bai-Perron structural breaks break-date confidence intervals (strucchange); accepts bare series regression formula. segmented_wrapper(): broken-line regression kink confidence intervals (segmented). envcpt_wrapper(): changepoints vs. trends vs. autocorrelation model selection (EnvCpt). fastcpd_wrapper(): modern fastcpd engine (fastcpd), covering mean/variance/meanvariance plus AR/ARMA/GARCH model changepoints.
